body:
This might be an issue of the ShapeCast's visual representation (gizmo).
It seems in Godot 3 the `target_position` is always global. So, the rotation of the Node (and what the gizmo shows) ends up being irrelevant/wrong for collision detection purposes. **

In other words, even if the gizmo clearly shows that no collision would happen, they may still be detected if the target position allows. This results in some nonsensical results, at least in editor - I didn't do code tests.

I checked the MRP (which had a problem opening the scene by the way) and managed to make all ShapeCasts detect collision.
It seems to be the same behavior in both Bullet and GodotPhysics. Also, did the auto-conversion to Godot 4 (using 4.4.dev3) and there it seems the rotation (and gizmo) have more correct behavior.

** It could also be the opposite: gizmo is correct, functionality isn't.

I think you're right about what's going on. Given the description of 'target_position', I think the gizmo is correct and the functionality isn't.

About the MRP issue, I assembled it by hand without realizing that copying a .project file into a subdirectory would invalidate the scene's file path. I don't know if I can replace the upload, but I'll try.
